data: Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.
Built by NPO Lavochkin, Luna 16 achieved the first fully robotic lunar sample return, bringing 101 g of soil back to Earth in September 1970.
First robotic lunar sample return; first non-American lunar samples
Last Soviet lunar mission; last uncrewed lunar landing for 37 years
The Soviet / Russian heavy-lift workhorse 1967-2012 — Salyut, Mir, Venera, Vega, Luna sample-return
First soft landing on another planet and first to transmit data from another planet's surface (Venus, 1970)
First human-made object to reach Mars surface; lander crashed (1971)
First soft landing on Mars; 14.5 s of surface transmission
Soviet 1973 Mars lander — first descent telemetry from Mars atmosphere (224 s, mostly corrupted)
First soft landing on another world
Last successful Soviet Moon mission — returned 170 g of Mare Crisium regolith 1976-08-22; last lunar sample return until Chang'e 5

The last Soviet lunar mission — and the last uncrewed Moon landing until China's Chang'e 3 in 2013: a gap of 37 years. Returned 170 g of samples including minerals containing water, foreshadowing the later discovery of lunar water ice.

First fully robotic sample return from another world — September 1970. Drilled into the lunar regolith with an articulated rotary drill, transferred 101 g of dust + small rock fragments into a sealed return capsule, then launched directly back to Earth without orbital rendezvous. Landed in Kazakhstan three days later. Two more Luna sample returns followed (Luna 20 in 1972, Luna 24 in 1976).
